questions.question: The session's practice map of Kransfontein is drawn at:
options: 1:50 000 with a contour interval of twenty metres, alongside a 1:10 000 orthophoto extract
A street-map scale with spot heights only

questions.question: Standing information worth reading in the map margin before any question includes:
options: The answers to the previous exercise
The sheet index, scale, contour interval and magnetic declination note

questions.question: Compared with the 1:50 000 sheet, the 1:10 000 orthophoto extract of the town centre is:
options: Five times larger in scale, showing photographic detail with contours overlaid

subtopics.title: Question 1 — Ten Quick Marks on the Maps

questions.question: A closed ring of contours with heights rising toward the centre represents:
A true bearing of 135 degrees from a point places the target roughly:
South African sheet index codes are built from:
options: The year of survey plus a serial number
The latitude and longitude of the degree square, plus letters locating a sixteenth of it
The population of the largest town on the sheet

subtopics.title: Question 2 — Map Codes, Grid References and the Ridge Path

questions.question: A complete coordinate answer for the beacon on Uitkyk must include:
options: Degrees, minutes and seconds with the hemisphere letters south and east
The beacon's height above sea level

questions.question: The walking path in block D4 rides a long nose of high ground running down between two tributary valleys. That landform is a:
An alphanumeric reference like D4 differs from a coordinate because it:
options: Locates a block on the map rather than fixing an exact point
Is more precise than a coordinate

subtopics.title: Question 3 — The Average Gradient Calculation, Step by Step

questions.question: In the practice gradient question, the vertical interval of 252,6 metres came from:
options: The contour interval of the map
1 512,6 metres at the beacon minus the 1 260-metre contour at A

questions.question: The measured 4,2 centimetres became a horizontal equivalent of 2 100 metres because:
options: At 1:50 000, each centimetre on the map represents 500 metres on the ground
The marking requires doubling every measurement
The path zigzags up the spur

questions.question: The practice marking accepts final answers from 1:8,1 to 1:8,5 because:
options: Rulers differ by a millimetre, so measurements from 4,1 to 4,3 centimetres are allowed
Gradient answers never need to be exact

questions.question: A candidate who writes only '1:8,3' with no working risks:
options: A penalty for using a ratio
Earning only the answer mark and gambling the stepwise method marks

questions.question: Vertical exaggeration is calculated as:
options: Vertical interval divided by horizontal equivalent
Spot height minus the lowest contour
Map distance multiplied by the scale
Vertical scale divided by horizontal scale, with the answer stated in times

questions.question: With a vertical scale of 1:5 000 and a horizontal scale of 1:50 000, the vertical exaggeration is:
Cross-sections use vertical exaggeration because:
options: It makes the drawing fit the page width
Drawn at true scale, the relief would be almost invisible on paper
Exaggeration changes the real steepness of the land
Rules of drawing forbid true-scale profiles

subtopics.title: Question 5 — Frost, Aspect and Streams: Theory Applied to the Map

questions.question: The vegetable farmer at M beside the Doringspruit fears clear, calm winter nights because:
options: Katabatic drainage ponds cold air on the valley floor, forming an inversion and a frost pocket
The river floods on clear nights
Anabatic winds carry hail down the valley
The town's heat island reaches the farm

questions.question: In the Southern Hemisphere, the warmer and historically more desirable residential slope is the one facing:
options: South, away from the midday sun

questions.question: Two first-order tributaries join, and their stream is later joined by another first-order stream. Below that second junction the stream is:
options: Second order, because only two streams of equal order raise the order

subtopics.title: Question 6 — GIS to Close the Practice Run

questions.question: The height 1 512,6 metres attached to the beacon on Uitkyk is an example of:
options: Attribute data describing a located feature

questions.question: Scale matters to a geographical query because:
options: All queries must use the smallest scale available
A street-corner question needs large-scale data like the 1:10 000 orthophoto; detail invisible at small scale cannot be queried
Larger scales always cover larger areas

questions.question: To identify housing at flood risk along the Doringspruit, a GIS analyst would:
options: Convert all layers to attribute tables
Buffer the river by a stated width and overlay the residential layer
Reduce the map to a smaller scale
